items.output: harbor renders Markdown into HTML. main.go handles the build and serve commands.

items.text:
**harbor** turns Markdown pages in `content/` into HTML using Go templates from `templates/`. The generated files go into `public/`.

The entry point is `main.go`. Its `main()` function chooses between building the site and serving the generated output. I only read files; nothing changed.

turns.prompt: Explain the entry point in more detail. Keep this read-only.

items.output: main() switches on os.Args[1]. build calls Site.Build(); serve uses http.FileServer for public/.

items.text:
`main()` dispatches on the first command-line argument:

- **`build`** creates a `Site` with the content, template, and output directories, then calls `Build()`. It prints how many pages were built.
- **`serve`** parses the preview address and serves `public/`.
- A missing or unknown command prints a usage message or error and exits.

The rendering work lives in `build.go`, not in this command dispatcher. Notice the call to `site.Build()` in the file beside this conversation.

**No files changed and no tests were run.**
